definitions.gloss: renting a room (in someone's house); subletting; lodging
definitions.explanation: Renting a room within someone else's home or existing space, rather than renting an entire apartment or house. Can also refer to borrowing part of a commercial space.

examples.japanese: {間借|まが}り⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{暮|く}らしている→暮らす：01937_kurasu⟧。
examples.english: I'm living in a rented room.

examples.japanese: ⟦{知人|ちじん}→知人：04056_chijin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{間借|まが}り⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: To rent a room at an acquaintance's house.

examples.japanese: ⟦{学生|がくせい}→学生：00610_gakusei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大家|おおや}さん→大家さん：26895_ooyasan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{二階|にかい}→二階：27513_nikai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{間借|まが}り⟦していた→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: When I was a student, I rented the second floor of the landlord's house.

notes:
Describes renting part of a space, not the whole unit. Traditionally refers to renting a room in someone's home, a common arrangement in older Japan and still seen today. Recently also used for businesses sharing commercial space (e.g., a pop-up restaurant operating inside another restaurant's space).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {間借|まが}り⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to rent a room / to sublet
- {間借|まが}り⟦{人|にん}→〜人：00658_nin⟧: lodger / tenant
- {間借|まが}り⟦{生活|せいかつ}→生活：01443_seikatsu⟧: life as a lodger
- {間借|まが}り⟦カレー→カレー：02898_karee⟧: pop-up curry restaurant (operating inside another space)
- {間借|まが}り⟦{営業|えいぎょう}→営業：01878_eigyou⟧: operating out of a shared/borrowed space

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{下宿|げしゅく}→下宿：01399_geshuku⟧: boarding house / lodging — a house specifically set up to take in boarders, with meals often included
- ⟦{賃貸|ちんたい}→賃貸：06081_chintai⟧: rental — renting an entire apartment or house
- ⟦{同居|どうきょ}→同居：09730_doukyo⟧: living together — sharing a home, but implies a closer relationship

MODERN USAGE:
The term {間借|まが}り has gained new life in the food industry, where {間借|まが}り⟦{営業|えいぎょう}→営業：01878_eigyou⟧ refers to a restaurant operating inside another establishment's space during off-hours, a popular low-cost way to start a food business.
